 There are 2 forms of intra-EU mobility for researchers.
 
-Short-term mobility: the researcher comes to the Netherlands to carry out research for a maximum of 180 days out of a 360-day period. No residence permit is required for short-term mobility. Your residence permit in the other country is also valid in the Netherlands.

--- corpus
+++ snapshot
@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@
 Intern or apprentice in the Netherlands
 
-Last update: 9 April 2026
+Last update: 22 May 2026
 
 In order to be an intern or apprentice in the Netherlands, you need a single permit (in Dutch: gecombineerde vergunning verblijf en arbeid or GVVA). The single permit is a combination of the residence permit and the work permit (in Dutch: tewerkstellingsvergunning or TWV). Find out what the requirements are and how to apply for the single permit.

 Paid employment: residence permit only
 
-Last update: 9 April 2026
+Last update: 22 May 2026
 
 You need a residence permit for paid employment in the Netherlands. You often have to apply for a single permit (in Dutch: Gecombineerde vergunning verblijf en arbeid or GVVA), but this is not always possible. Then you can apply for a residence permit for paid employment. Find out what the requirements are and how to apply for the residence permit.
